title: Container Bookings: loading guarantee premium refund and other effects of a cancellation
content:
## Policy clause
When a Container Bookings booking that paid a loading guarantee premium is cancelled at least the tier's premium refund notice in calendar days before the ETD, the premium entry is refunded in full through a refund entry recorded as a premium refund that references that premium entry; cancelled later, the premium is kept. Premium refunds are not goodwill and never count toward the customer's goodwill waiver quota.

The cancellation also voids the booking's draft transport document, and the export free-time record of the booking is cancelled only when no empty container has been picked up under it, as the demurrage and detention product rules provide.

## Condition, judgement, result
| Condition on the cancelled booking | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A loading guarantee premium was charged, and the cancellation is at least the notice before ETD | refund due | full premium refunded, referencing the premium entry |
| A loading guarantee premium was charged, and the cancellation is later than that | refund not due | premium kept |
| An empty container has been picked up under the export free-time record | record stays | the free-time record is not cancelled |
| No empty container has been picked up | record cancelled | the free-time record is cancelled |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical notice)
*Hypothetical notice of 9 calendar days, for illustration only:* for an ETD of 20 October, a cancellation on 11 October is exactly 9 days before and the premium is refunded; a cancellation on 12 October is 8 days before and the premium is kept.

## Points of judgement
**Is the refund a partial amount?** No. The premium entry is refunded in full.

**Does the refund use up one of the customer's goodwill waivers?** No. A premium refund is not goodwill and is never counted in the goodwill quota.
